diagnosis.historical_failure: phase4-e2e-local.log records desktop: fixed bottom element overlaps main content (true !== false).
diagnosis.old_test_cause: git diff of verify_release_candidate.mjs shows the previous assertion compared vertical bounds only. A full-height fixed sidebar touches the viewport bottom and vertically intersects main content even when its right edge equals the main content's left edge.
diagnosis.current_guard: rectanglesOverlap uses strict intersection on left/right and top/bottom; verify_release_candidate.mjs now applies it to DOMRect JSON and includes tablet 768x1024 between desktop 1280x800 and mobile 375x667.
diagnosis.geometry_fixture: sidebar [0,256] adjacent to main [256,1280] is false; crossing bottom bar [256,1280] is true; offscreen mobile drawer [-256,0] adjacent to main [0,375] is false.
diagnosis.conclusion: The reported desktop failure is explained by a false-positive vertical-only assertion, not established visual occlusion. Existing CSS places the sidebar in a separate grid column. A live browser inspection is still needed to exclude every other fixed-element scenario.
diagnosis.safe_fix: Keep full two-axis rectangle intersection and regression fixtures; do not move or remove the fixed sidebar merely to satisfy the old assertion. If a later live DOM measurement identifies a genuinely covering element, fix that element's placement and add a failing browser regression before changing CSS.
